stage1.impression: This is a competent night street view of a dark steel shopfront with a warm, wood-lined room behind the glass. It still reads as CG. The pavement and the neighbour's stucco are smooth and flat. The steel cladding shows a repeated blotchy grunge with bright chrome flecks rather than a soft blackened patina. The pale flats above are brighter than the bar, and the frame has no blue-hour air at all: everything is the same amber, and no EARF speaker reads as a hero from the street. As it stands a magazine would see a generic, handsome bar front rather than a specific place. Only the fogged dancing-woman lightbox gives it an identity, and the etched name is too faint to read.

blocking_9: Real blue hour: cool ambient on the street, the stucco and the flats, so the warm room is the only warm thing in the frame (outside surfaces b_median >= r_median)
The lit room is the brightest, most legible area in the frame, brighter than the flats above and the lightbox
At least one Atmosphere speaker, or its lit niche or altar, is visible and readable through the glass as the hero
The blackened steel reads as real patinated steel (soft uneven sheen, sharp edges, no tiled grunge or chrome flecks)
The pavement and the neighbouring facade carry real texture: joints, kerb grime, stains, a wet sheen that varies
The etched name reads as EARF in the glass at a glance
Some sign of life at the window or the counter (a figure, a coat or a glass near the glass) and some atmosphere in the street air

defects.what: The flats above are lit to median 85, about three times the room's brightness, and pull the eye away from the shop. The balconies look like flat, clean CG boxes.
The neighbour's stucco is a smooth, uniform CG surface with an amber cast (r 61, b 35), nothing like blue hour. The shuttered window is a flat texture.
The steel cladding panels repeat one grunge map with bright specular flecks. It reads as a decal, not blackened steel.
The same tiled, flecked steel texture on the door jamb.
The stallriser is a crushed dark band (median 13) with the same repeating tile texture.
The pavement and kerb are flat, untextured planes: no joints, grime or variation. The kerb is a perfect extruded edge.
The etched name is a faint ghost that reads as 'EAAF' or a smudge.
The interior is monochrome orange (b_median 7). Blacks block up to a pure orange-brown and the room's materials don't separate.
The lightbox (median 94) outshines the room behind the glass and pulls toward pink-beige.
The vestibule's speaker-like object is tiny, grey and indistinct. No product reads as the hero.
A cut-off red object at the left edge of the frame.

changes.problem: The card calls for blue hour, but the whole frame is graded amber, so outside and inside don't contrast and the shot loses its reason to exist.

evidence.measured: neighbour wall r_median 61, g 44, b 35; street [0,640,1200,800] r 47, b 32

change.to: 3300 K white balance, street lamps 4000 K, so the 2400-2600 K room stays amber and the outside goes cool blue-grey

changes.expected: Stucco and pavement read neutral-to-cool blue, and the shop window glows warm against them as the frame's one warm area.

changes.problem: The street lamps light the flats above far brighter than the shop, so the eye lands on the balconies.

change.to: 50 W, and placed below the first-floor line so the flats fall off upward

changes.expected: The flats sit around median 35 to 45 and darken toward the top of the frame, and the shopfront band becomes the brightest zone.

changes.problem: The room behind the glass is too dim and too orange to read as a place: its counter, record wall and fir separate only as orange shapes.

change.setting: Domes' downlights / record wall spots / render.exposure
change.to: 450 W / 120 W / exposure 2.3 (after c1's white-balance change)

changes.expected: Interior median rises to 35 to 45 with legible fir, spines and counter edge, and blue stays above crush (b_median >= 12).

changes.problem: The frosted lightbox is the brightest thing in the window and competes with the room and the product.

change.to: 0.5, and the frosted acrylic slightly rougher so the glow is even edge to edge

changes.expected: The lightbox sits about one stop above the room rather than four, so the silhouette remains the identity and the room reads past it.

changes.problem: The blackened-steel cladding shows a tiled grunge with chrome-bright flecks, which reads as a game texture.

evidence.measured: lum_range 29.9 with isolated highlight specks on a median-22 field; the same pattern repeats panel to panel at 1:1

change.from: high-contrast mottled patina, low roughness flecks
change.to: near-black brownish patina, roughness 0.45 to 0.6 varied by a large-scale noise, the patina map scaled about 3x and rotated per panel, crisp lighter edges on panel arrises

changes.expected: The cladding reads as one soft, uneven, near-black sheen, with no repeated blotches and no sparkle.

changes.problem: The pavement, kerb and neighbouring stucco are smooth, uniform CG planes.

evidence.measured: lum_range 74 is almost all from the reflected window pools. The surface itself is flat, with no joints or grime at 1:1

change.setting: street pavement and neighbour facade finish
change.to: concrete paver joints about 1.2 m apart, kerb grime and a chipped arris, damp patches with varying roughness (0.15 to 0.6), and stucco with fine bump and faint water staining

changes.expected: The street reads as a real San Francisco sidewalk, and the window's reflection breaks up across the damp patches.

changes.problem: The etched name in the glass is a faint, unreadable ghost.

evidence.measured: letters lift only slightly off the room behind and read as 'EAAF'

changes.expected: EARF reads at a glance as frosted letters on the glass, still quieter than the lightbox.

changes.problem: The aim and framing give a quarter of the frame to a dead neighbour wall and cut the flats arbitrarily, while no speaker is visible through the glass.

evidence.measured: about 22% of the frame width is neighbour wall at lum_median 47 with no content

change.to: position about [-10.0, 1.5, 1.5], target [6, 3.0, 1.6] so the line of sight runs through the glass toward the altar or the back-bar niches, lens 40 mm, verticals kept level; add a few seconds of street haze

changes.expected: The shopfront fills the frame edge to edge. An Atmosphere speaker, lit by its altar spots, reads through the glass as the hero, and the flats become a strip at the top.

out_of_scope.request: Make the Smoke-tinted speakers or their lamps carry more colour so the product reads from the street
out_of_scope.why: The products' colour and tint are fixed by the card. Visibility has to come from camera and light (c8, the altar spots).

out_of_scope.request: Make the flats' balconies less boxy and the upper facade more characterful
out_of_scope.why: The building above is part of the shopfront and site as proposed, so it is a design or asset change rather than a photographic one.

out_of_scope.request: Put a person in the window or at the counter as a sign of life
out_of_scope.why: People are not among the card's small props. Ask the owner whether a figure is allowed.
